draft.title: Termination management
card: Termination is when employment ends. A business must manage it fairly and follow the law, whoever ends the job.
the employee chooses to leave. Retirement is also the employee's choice, when they stop working, usually later in life.
the employer ends the job because the role is no longer needed, for example after new technology replaces it. It is not about the worker's performance.
the employer ends the job because of the employee's conduct or performance. The business must follow a fair process and give notice where required.
draft.remember: Termination can start with the employee or the business, and the business has duties either way.

a.q: Sam's employer closes a packing line, so Sam's job no longer exists. Sam's work was good. Which type of termination is this?
a.why: The employer ended the job because the role is no longer needed, which is redundancy. Dismissal is the tempting option, but it relates to conduct or performance, and Sam's work was good.
a.clue: Ask why the job ended: the person or the role?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Ballarat. She ends a baker's job after repeated warnings about arriving late. Which type of termination is this, and why?
opts: Dismissal, because it is about the baker's conduct
Redundancy, because the employer ended the job
Resignation, because the baker chose to be late
Dismissal, because the baker chose to leave the job
b.why: The employer ended the job because of the employee's conduct, so it is dismissal. Redundancy is tempting because the employer also ends that job, but redundancy is about the role no longer being needed, not the worker's behaviour.
b.clue: Look at the reason the employer gives for ending the job.

b.best: Dismissal, because it is about the baker's conduct
